text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000136 bills 99215 well above risk-adjusted expectation in every complexity band, but the few documented 99215 charts mostly support the billed level, so the record is too thin to call.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The 99215 excess is not explained by panel acuity: the provider's 99215 share runs roughly double the all-provider share in every complexity band, including 0–1 condition patients, and the low-complexity sample includes visits with single routine diagnoses such as C0069809 (I10 only) and C0070172 (J06.9). Against that, only 6 of the documented claims were 99215s, and just one (C0070485, a 0-condition N39.0 visit documented at moderate MDM) fell below the billed level, far under the comparison rate, which is too small a sample to confirm or clear the pattern. The supporting charts carry their own caution: C0070424, a 1-condition hyperlipidemia/back-pain visit, is documented at high MDM with no minutes recorded, and the code-flagged gap of notes claiming moderate-or-higher data review without a lab or test line on the claim is weak evidence that notes may be templated or inflated rather than proof. A reviewer should first request additional 99215 charts, prioritizing the 0–1 condition claims in the low-complexity sample, and the missing audit trail to check whether high-MDM notes such as C0070142 and C0070424 reflect actual work performed."}
